short: Hydrogen storage behavior of Mg-based alloy catalyzed by car
title: Hydrogen storage behavior of Mg-based alloy catalyzed by carbon-cobalt composites

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Mg-based hydrogen storage alloys absorb and desorb hydrogen too slowly and need high temperatures. A defect-rich carbon-cobalt composite (C@Co) should catalyse nucleation and hydrogen diffusion in a Mg-RE alloy and speed its de/hydrogenation.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (PRC/synthesis), n8 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Carbon nanosheets of C@Co are highly defective (ID/IG about 0.97), a source of catalytic sites. C@Co does not react with the alloy: milled C10 shows only C0's phases plus Co, and Co persists after de/hydrogenation.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Defects in the carbon nanosheets act as nucleation sites for Mg/MgH2. Carbon nanosheets embedded in the alloy particles provide channels for hydrogen diffusion through MgH2.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (MEC/pathway), n12 (MEC/pathway), n13 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n16 (PRP/diagnostic), n17 (MEC/identification), n18 (PRP/value), n19 (PRP/value). Premises: Defects in carbon supply catalytic active sites for nucleation in de/hydrogenation and lower the activation energy; Hydrogenation of Mg runs in two stages: the first nucleation-controlled, the second diffusion-controlled; Mg hydride desorption has two rate-limiting steps: Mg nucleation and recombination of H atoms on the Mg surface; JMAK exponent value maps to the rate-controlling step of Mg/MgH2 desorption (surface control vs nucleation and growth)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: C10 is fully activated in the first hydrogenation cycle at 360 C, whereas C0 needs three cycles

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: C@Co is an inert catalyst that improves Mg90Ce5Y5 de/hydrogenation kinetics and lowers Ea through a C (nucleation, diffusion) plus Co (H recombination) synergy, not through thermodynamics

nodes.title: PHYS:surfacearea, F6, F7
nodes.head: Second (diffusion-controlled) absorption stage lasts 66 min for C0 and 11 min for C10 at 360 C. Isothermal absorption at 250-100 C: C10 curves rise to their plateau faster than C0 at every temperature.
nodes.solves: C@Co speeds hydrogen absorption: R10min of C10 exceeds C0 at 250-100 C
nodes.op: compare across conditions, replot derived series
nodes.note: interval drawn by authors between dashed lines; not a listed annotation string values printed on bars (not listed annotations); legend C0/C10 on panel
nodes.detail: o20: Second (diffusion-controlled) absorption stage lasts 66 min for C0 and 11 min for C10 at 360 C; o21: Isothermal absorption at 250-100 C: C10 curves rise to their plateau faster than C0 at every temperature; o23: R10min is higher for C10 than C0 at every temperature: 95.2 vs 81.7 (250), 84 vs 58.9 (200), 64.1 vs 52 (150), 36.3 vs 25.2 % (100 C)
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n14 (o20, o21, o23).

nodes.title: THERMAL:DSC, F12, F8
nodes.head: Complete desorption at 300 C takes ~150 min for C0 but ~11 min for C10; C10 finishes in <40 min even at 280 C vs ~450 min for C0. DSC endothermic MgH2 peak at 396.5 C (C0) vs 338.5 C (C10); onset 341.0 vs 267.0 C
nodes.solves: C@Co speeds hydrogen desorption: DSC peak falls from 396.5 to 338.5 C and onset from 341.0 to 267.0 C
nodes.note: text gives 338 C; figure 338.5 C. Legend writes 'Co@C' for the C@Co additive
nodes.detail: o24: Complete desorption at 300 C takes ~150 min for C0 but ~11 min for C10; C10 finishes in <40 min even at 280 C vs ~450 min for C0; o25: DSC endothermic MgH2 peak at 396.5 C (C0) vs 338.5 C (C10); onset 341.0 vs 267.0 C
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n15 (o24, o25).

nodes.note: F9 caption says 'hydrogenated' alloys but axes and linked text concern desorption; slopes of the four lines per panel look parallel, consistent with one eta

nodes.title: THERMAL:DSC, F11, F12
nodes.head: PCT at 320-360 C: one flat plateau per temperature; C10 plateaus lie at nearly the same pressures as C0 (~0.15, 0.27, 0.45 MPa). Van't Hoff fits: desorption dH = 83.3 kJ/mol (C0) vs 81.7 kJ/mol (C10); absorption -80.0 vs -82.5 kJ/mol.
nodes.solves: C@Co leaves the thermodynamics nearly unchanged: plateau pressures and desorption enthalpy (83.3 vs 81.7 kJ/mol) barely differ
nodes.note: figure temperatures are 360/340/320 C (text says 360, 320, 320 C); a small absorption-desorption offset is visible, not zero hysteresis; C10 capacity ~4.8 vs ~5.2 wt% in panel d the subscripts are swapped: the Absorption block reads dH_des = -82.5 and the Desorption block dH_abs = 81.7; slopes x R reproduce the values
nodes.detail: o28: PCT at 320-360 C: one flat plateau per temperature; C10 plateaus lie at nearly the same pressures as C0 (~0.15, 0.27, 0.45 MPa); o29: Van't Hoff fits: desorption dH = 83.3 kJ/mol (C0) vs 81.7 kJ/mol (C10); absorption -80.0 vs -82.5 kJ/mol; o30: DSC reaction heat 616.3 J/g (C0) vs 603.1 J/g (C10)

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: At 360 C, C0's first hydrogenation reaches only ~3.2 wt% in 180 min while cycles 2-3 saturate; C10's first cycle saturates within ~5 min like cycles 2-3
nodes.solves: C10 is fully activated in the first hydrogenation cycle at 360 C, whereas C0 needs three cycles
nodes.note: C10 first cycle plateaus at ~5.2 wt% but cycles 2-3 only ~4.7 wt% (capacity drop after cycle 1, not discussed)
